status: RUNNING again since 00:20 on 11-18 (Prasann) under new rules: LoRA and fixed data re-mixes count as the dense baseline, so only dynamic FLOP dropping during training is a method; the reference is dense full fine-tuning; a method counts only at the deepest loss the dense baseline reaches; the search starts from drop settings that track dense per step at a higher step cost and lowers the step cost from there. Dense full fine-tune reference: 16k CE 0.114 / 0.119 on two seeds after one epoch (1,982 PF). Qualifying result so far: the keep ramp (one cut after block 7, keep share 20% to 90% over training, full fine-tune) matches dense on both seeds (0.113 / 0.119) at 0.64x the step cost, 1.57-1.59x fewer FLOPs at the dense final loss. Constant budgets do not reach the dense final loss in one epoch: LoRA with 50% / 20% / 7% over three cuts holds dense LoRA's loss at 0.29x per step and reaches dense full fine-tune's step-350 level at about 3x. Diagnosis: the loss gap of aggressive drops is the missing gradient of dropped tokens, not the truncated context. Headline (finished runs with complete schedules, 16k CE on 320 rows; two seeds at 495, 991 and 1,980 PF, one seed at 3,975 PF): token dropping with LoRA and a 50% / 20% / 7% keep over three cuts needs 2.3x, 2.1x and 2.4x fewer FLOPs than the dense frontier (dense full fine-tune and dense LoRA at every budget up to 7,934 PF) at 495, 991 and 1,980 PF, and 1.9-2.0x at 3,975 PF on the 16x pool; the gain does not shrink with data over an 8-fold range of budgets. That is far from the 10-20x target: every attempt to go below about 0.3x dense per step (smaller keep shares, an earlier first cut, more stages, frozen early blocks, keep schedules, gradient compensation) lost per FLOP. In flight: runs at 3,964 PF on a 16x pool, and input document subsampling combined with the token drop.
setup: Each method trains with its own forward, optimiser and real LR schedule on the same first batches of the pool (16 rows/step, 2 GPUs).

At fixed steps the dense forward (full context, no dropping, adapters on) is scored on held-out rows from the CTC-suite eval files: teacher-forced answer CE, 16 rows per task and length (4k, 8k, 16k) except reorder at 16k, where only 8 eval rows fit in 16,384 tokens; eval_size 184.

Score = training FLOPs the dense reference needs to reach a loss level divided by the FLOPs the method needs to reach the same level, on the mean loss and on the worst task. Peak GPU memory is logged per step.
One iteration is under 15 minutes. Every 2-3 hours the most promising methods get a larger FLOP-matched training run with generation-graded evals.

Data caveats: the 16k training cells use fewer documents per row than the eval (contradiction 324 vs 379, outlier 96 vs 111, reorder 90 vs 116) so rows fit in 16,384 tokens; the 16k held-out rows are the short tail of the eval rung (70, 303, 8 and 497 of 500 rows fit for contradiction, outlier, reorder, qdmatch_nq). About 46% of the documents in a qdmatch_nq held-out row also occur in training rows (no gold overlap, no prompt overlap).

For runs that stop before reaching a reference level, the table also gives iso-loss ratios at the run's own final loss: FLOPs the dense-LoRA reference (and the recipe) need to reach that loss divided by the run's FLOPs. These are generous to a run whose final loss is shallow, because the reference curves are only probed every 10-25 steps.

Deep comparisons (from 11-17 11:30) use the full-epoch dense-LoRA curve (488 steps, probes every 50) as the reference and give the FLOP ratio at fixed held-out CE levels 0.160 / 0.140 / 0.125 / 0.115 / 0.105 / 0.095.
Memory: values logged by the proxy before 11-17 13:10 were wrong (the peak was reset before being read) and are not shown; the fix is merged. Valid measurements are in the memory idea and the log.
From 11-18 the held-out set is heldout_v3: 320 rows at 16k (gen16k + rung16k) plus 64 rows at 4k / 8k; the 16k mean is the primary number (eval_size 320, below 500).

Memory goal restated by Prasann: not savings at 16k but algorithms that keep memory nearly flat at 256k, 1M tokens or longer. New agent: memory scaling law with length, then chunked early blocks with a fixed kept-token budget.

Priority changed to the 16k held-out loss and to ideas that gain more as rows get longer. On the 16k rows alone (56 rows, noisy) the plain recipe is 2.1-2.7x vs dense LoRA and the short-heavy pools are only about 1.1-1.2x ahead of it (1.8-2.1x ahead at 4k). A larger 16k held-out set is being built (48 fresh in-range rows and 32 uncapped 16k-rung eval rows per task); references will be rerun on it. New idea started: per-length FLOP breakdown and document-local attention in the early blocks.
Loop paused by a usage limit until 11:20; cluster jobs finished on their own. A recurring heartbeat now restarts the loop after a limit resets.

Overnight results scored. Recipe through the full epoch: 1.9-2.2x at every loss level (two seeds). Recipe on mtbmix50: 2.4-3.0x; on mtbmix80: 3.1-3.4x at CE 0.125 (2.7-4.4x across levels and seeds). Loss-per-cost cell sampling: 2.3-2.6x on the main pool, 3.2-3.7x on the 50/50 pool (one seed). Rows <= 5k: 3.2-3.4x until it plateaus at 0.119. Dense LoRA on the 50/50 pool with token-budget batches: 1.4-1.5x. Multi-question rows: 1.8-2.1x on the main pool, below the plain recipe. Gold-aware keep on the 50/50 pool: no gain over the recipe on that pool. Detached context from block 16 only: far behind (0.207 vs 0.145 at 131 PF).

First larger validation started: full-epoch dense LoRA (three FLOP budgets), recipe (two seeds) and dense full FT on mtb16k with generation-graded evals at 4k / 8k / 16k; plus full-epoch dense-loss curves for dense LoRA and the recipe.

Short-row pools: recipe on the 50/50 and 80/20 mixes is 1.25x the recipe at matched loss; short rows alone 0.74x; dense LoRA on any of them is behind the recipe. Detached context: negative (context forward-only without drops 0.15x of the recipe's efficiency; every 4th step dense 0.44x). Early-exit-loss selection: negative (ridge router is better at equal keep). Input-level token exit at ratio 0.05-0.10 does not train from the standard or the drop-CPT base. Dense LoRA at LR 2e-5 is a slightly better reference (0.126 vs 0.131 at step 100); LR 4e-5 is worse.
Two ideas closed as negative: frozen no-grad prefix with earlier cuts, and FFN skip for context tokens. Both show that blocks 0-6 need every token, every FFN and their own gradient.

Short-row pools built (mean row 1.6k / 3.1k / 5.4k tokens vs 9.1k) and running on Beaker with dense LoRA and the recipe. Detached-context screen moved to Beaker. Reorder is the task every cheap arm loses on (0.45-0.60 vs 0.33).

Lambda (2 x A100 per run) and Beaker (2 x H100 per run) staged and verified: step-0 loss matches Berkeley. Six Beaker jobs launched (LR and rows-per-step sweeps, dense-LoRA reference LR check, keep ladder down to 2% / 1%).

References done: dense full FT 0.135 and dense LoRA 0.131 held-out CE at step 100; recipe 0.125 at step 200 for 0.22x dense per step. Reorder dominates the mean loss (about 0.33 for all three; the other tasks 0.04-0.11).
CPT search: a usable token-exit CPT base (dropstruct, tokens leave from block 8, 64M CPT tokens) and its dense-CPT control exist and are staged; the 1B-token FFN-drop CPT base was deleted on 10-30.

Pool mtb16k and held-out v2 final after one rebuild (16k cells regenerated with fewer documents so rows fit in 16,384 tokens). References and baselines launched on 6 GPUs; all 8 preemptive_high GPUs in use.

Seven idea agents started (no-grad prefix + early cuts, gold-aware stochastic keep, early-layer loss selection, detached context, FLOP-aware row sampling, FFN skip for context tokens, token-drop CPT base search). Staging agents started for Lambda and Beaker.
Loop requested: tasks switched to contradiction, outlier, reorder, qdmatch_nq at 4k-16k; target 10-20x FLOPs and 5-10x less peak memory.
